newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland sells Handlowy long-term investor tranche.
newsitem.headline: Poland sells Handlowy long-term investor tranche.

text.p: Poland concluded on Wednesday the sale of Bank Handlowy SA shares and bonds in its 24-percent long-term investor tranche to J.P. Morgan & Co Inc, Zurich Insurance Co and Swedbank, Handlowy said in a statement.

It said the state treasury sold the three investors a total of 16,874,000 shares and 5,446,000 convertible bonds exchangeable for one share each. The securities will jointly represent a 24-percent equity in Handlowy's equity diluted by a 28-million convertible bond issue.
JP Morgan and its subsidiaries were buying 9,602,500 shares and 1,557,500 convertible bonds or 12 percent.

Zurich Insurance Co or its subsidiaries were buying 4,022,500 shares and 1,557,500 bonds, representing a six percent stake, and Swedbank was getting 3,249,000 shares and 2,331,000 bonds also amounting to six percent.
Handlowy now has 65 million shares and 28 million convertible bonds. A total of 38.25 million shares were sold earlier this month in a heavily oversubscribed public offering priced at 35 zlotys.

The three investors would pay 20 zlotys on the day of the closing of the transaction due by the end of this year, 11.4 zlotys payable three years after the deal and a premium in the fourth year representing a portion of a possible rise in Handlowy's market value.

Handlowy said that under the conditions of the sale the investors agreed to hold one-third of the purchased securities for at least 540 days after the transaction, one-third for 810 days and one-third for three years.
